answer: Trust propagates from anchored attestations through bounded-length random walks on the graph, so voting weight reflects trusted reachability rather than self-asserted identities. A sybil cluster connected to honest nodes by a sparse external cut has low conductance: the cut limits trusted walk flow into the cluster, bounding its aggregate voting weight over a fixed walk horizon. A relic mirror perched on a ledge cannot evade that bound without creating attestations across the cut.
